findings.title: The new abstract method breaks existing custom OAuth2 grant providers at startup
findings.body: Adding `getShortcut()` as an abstract interface method is binary-incompatible with OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations compiled against the previous release. The new default token-context factory invokes this method for every registered OAuth2 grant factory during post-initialization, so an existing extension without the method will throw AbstractMethodError and prevent the server from starting. Provide a default/compatibility implementation and handle unrecognized legacy grants as unknown, or otherwise avoid invoking the new method on old implementations.

findings.title: Grant shortcut lengths accepted by the factory cannot be decoded
findings.body: The decoder hard-codes a six-character context, which requires a two-character grant shortcut, but OAuth2GrantTypeFactory documents shortcuts as usually three letters and the factory does not validate their length. A custom grant returning (for example) `foo` will mint IDs such as `onrtfoo:<uuid>`, then getTokenContextFromTokenId will reject those same IDs with "Expected length of 6." Require exactly two-character shortcuts during factory initialization and document that requirement, or make the encoding self-delimiting.

findings.title: rawTokenId is never null-checked
findings.body: This line checks `grantType` a second time instead of checking `rawTokenId`, despite the error message claiming that a null raw token ID is prohibited. A caller of this public context API can therefore construct a context with a null raw ID, and the default encoder will serialize it as the literal string `:null` rather than rejecting an invalid token ID. Check `rawTokenId` here.

findings.title: The access-token event matcher does not validate the expected grant shortcut
findings.body: The matcher extracts characters 3-4 even though the grant shortcut occupies characters 4-5 of the six-character prefix, and it returns false when the extracted value equals the expected shortcut. For example, `onrtac:<uuid>` with expected `ac` extracts `ta` and passes; a token with a different grant shortcut also passes in the normal cases. Consequently the updated event assertions do not catch regressions in grant-type encoding. Compare `substring(4, 6)` to the expected shortcut positively, after validating the prefix length.
